processes.name: Sand casting
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Metals › Non-ferrous › Nickel and cobalt alloys
processes.note: Molten metal poured into a sand mould made round a pattern. Any size, cheap tooling, rough surface; cores make hollow parts.

processes.name: Die casting (high pressure)
processes.note: Low-melting alloys injected into a steel die. Thin walls, fine detail and good finish; the die pays off only over large batches.

processes.name: Investment casting
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Metals › Non-ferrous › Nickel and cobalt alloys
processes.note: A wax pattern coated in ceramic, melted out, and the shell filled. Complex shapes in high-melting alloys with a good finish.

processes.name: Permanent mould casting (gravity die)
processes.note: Metal poured by gravity into a reusable metal mould: better finish and properties than sand, for medium batches.

processes.name: Injection moulding
processes.note: Molten polymer forced into a cooled steel mould. Complex, accurate parts at a high rate; the mould needs large batches.

processes.name: Blow moulding
processes.note: A hot tube of polymer blown against a mould: bottles, tanks and ducts.

processes.name: Extrusion (polymers)
processes.note: Polymer pushed through a die: pipe, profile, sheet and film of constant section.

processes.name: Thermoforming
processes.note: Heated sheet drawn over a mould by vacuum or pressure: trays, panels, covers and packaging.

processes.name: Rotational moulding
processes.note: Polymer powder tumbled in a heated mould: large hollow parts such as tanks and kayaks, with cheap tooling.

processes.name: Compression moulding
processes.note: A charge pressed and cured in a heated mould: thermosets, rubber and sheet moulding compound.

processes.name: Resin casting
processes.note: Liquid resin (epoxy, polyester, polyurethane) poured into a mould and cured. Cheap tooling for few parts.

processes.name: Closed-die forging
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Metals › Non-ferrous › Nickel and cobalt alloys
processes.note: Hot metal hammered or pressed between shaped dies: strong parts with a good grain flow.

processes.name: Rolling
processes.note: Metal squeezed between rolls into plate, sheet, foil, bar and sections. Mostly done at the mill: buy stock.

processes.name: Extrusion (metals)
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
processes.note: A billet pushed through a die: long profiles of constant section, hollow or solid; aluminium above all.

processes.name: Sheet stamping and deep drawing
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Metals › Non-ferrous › Nickel and cobalt alloys
processes.note: Sheet cut, bent and drawn in press tools: car bodies, cans, brackets. Fast, but the tools are costly.

processes.name: Sheet bending (press brake)
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Metals › Non-ferrous › Nickel and cobalt alloys
processes.note: Cut sheet folded along straight lines with standard tools: enclosures, brackets and panels in small batches.

processes.name: Powder pressing and sintering
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
processes.note: Powder pressed in a die and sintered: gears, bushes, cutting tips and technical ceramics, near net shape.

processes.name: Metal injection moulding
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Metals › Non-ferrous › Nickel and cobalt alloys
processes.note: Metal powder in a binder moulded like a polymer, then debound and sintered: small, complex metal parts in large numbers.

processes.name: Slip casting (ceramics)
processes.note: A slurry poured into a porous plaster mould, dried and fired: sanitary ware, crucibles and complex ceramic shapes.

processes.name: Glass pressing and blowing
processes.note: Hot glass pressed or blown in a mould: bottles, lenses, lamp bulbs and tableware.

processes.name: Hand lay-up
processes.note: Fibre mat or cloth laid in an open mould and wetted with resin: boat hulls, panels and one-offs.

processes.name: Prepreg and autoclave
processes.note: Pre-impregnated plies laid up and cured under heat and pressure: the highest-quality aerospace and racing parts.

processes.name: Resin transfer moulding
processes.note: Dry fibre placed in a closed mould and resin injected: good finish on both faces, medium batches.

processes.name: Filament winding
processes.note: Resin-wetted fibre wound round a rotating mandrel: pipes, pressure vessels and drive shafts.

processes.name: Pultrusion
processes.note: Fibre pulled through a resin bath and a heated die: constant-section profiles, rods and ladders.

processes.name: Sawing and routing (wood)
processes.note: Sawing, planing and CNC routing of timber and boards.

processes.name: Turning
fam: Ceramics and glasses › Technical ceramics › Carbon
processes.note: A rotating workpiece cut by a single-point tool: shafts, pins, bushes and anything round. Charge the chips as “machined away” in the eco audit.

processes.name: Milling
fam: Ceramics and glasses › Technical ceramics › Carbon
processes.note: Rotating cutters remove material: flat faces, pockets, slots and free-form shapes on CNC machines.

processes.name: Grinding
processes.note: Abrasive wheels remove a little material for the finest tolerance and finish, also on hard steels and ceramics.

processes.name: Electrical discharge machining
fam: Ceramics and glasses › Technical ceramics › Carbides
processes.note: Sparks erode any conductive material, however hard: dies, moulds and fine slots. Slow.

processes.name: Laser cutting
processes.note: A focused laser cuts sheet and plate to any outline, with no tooling.

processes.name: Water-jet cutting
processes.note: A jet of water and abrasive cuts almost any material, cold, to any outline.

processes.name: Powder-bed fusion (metals)
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Metals › Non-ferrous › Nickel and cobalt alloys
processes.note: A laser or electron beam melts powder layer by layer: complex metal parts, lattices and internal channels, with no tooling.

processes.name: Material extrusion (3D printing)
processes.note: A filament melted and laid down layer by layer: prototypes, jigs and one-off parts.

processes.name: Vat photopolymerisation (resin)
processes.note: A light source cures liquid resin layer by layer: fine detail and a smooth surface.

processes.name: Powder-bed fusion (polymers)
processes.note: A laser sinters polyamide powder layer by layer: strong functional parts with no supports.

processes.name: Binder jetting
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
processes.note: A binder printed into powder, then sintered: metal and ceramic parts in larger numbers than powder-bed fusion.

processes.name: Arc welding (MIG, TIG)
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Metals › Non-ferrous › Nickel and cobalt alloys
processes.note: The workhorse of metal joining: strong, sealed joints; heat distorts thin parts and alters the metal near the weld.

processes.name: Laser welding
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Metals › Non-ferrous › Nickel and cobalt alloys
processes.note: A narrow, deep weld with little heat: precise, fast and automated.

processes.name: Friction stir welding
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
processes.note: A rotating tool stirs the two edges together without melting: excellent on aluminium alloys that are hard to fusion-weld.

processes.name: Resistance spot welding
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
processes.note: Overlapping sheets fused at spots by current: car bodies and sheet assemblies.

processes.name: Brazing
processes.note: A filler that melts above 450 °C joins without melting the parts: dissimilar metals, carbide tips and ceramic-to-metal seals.

processes.name: Soldering
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
processes.note: A low-melting filler: electrical joints, plumbing and fine assemblies; weak above about 150 °C.

processes.name: Adhesive bonding
processes.note: Glue spreads the load over the whole joint and joins almost anything to anything; surface preparation matters, and heat limits it.

processes.name: Bolts, screws and rivets
processes.note: Mechanical fastening: bolts and screws can be undone for repair and recycling; rivets are permanent but need no heat.

processes.name: Snap fits
processes.note: Moulded-in hooks: assembly without tools or fasteners, and easy disassembly.

processes.name: Plastic welding (ultrasonic, hot plate)
processes.note: Thermoplastics melted at the joint and fused: sealed, permanent joints in seconds.

processes.name: Painting
processes.note: Liquid paint sprayed or brushed: colour and protection for almost anything.

processes.name: Powder coating
processes.note: Charged powder sprayed and baked: a thick, tough finish on metal with no solvent.

processes.name: Anodising
processes.note: A hard oxide grown on the surface, which can be dyed: aluminium above all.

processes.name: Electroplating
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
processes.note: A thin metal layer (zinc, nickel, chromium, gold) deposited from solution; ABS can be plated after etching.

processes.name: Hot-dip galvanising
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
processes.note: Steel dipped in molten zinc: decades of rust protection outdoors.

processes.name: Hard coating (PVD, CVD)
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Ceramics and glasses › Technical ceramics › Carbides
processes.note: A few micrometres of titanium nitride or similar: cutting tools, moulds and decorative parts.

processes.name: Polishing
processes.note: Abrasives and compounds give a smooth, bright surface.

processes.name: Heat treatment
fam: Metals › Ferrous › Carbon and low-alloy steels
Metals › Non-ferrous › Nickel and cobalt alloys
processes.note: Hardening, tempering, solution treatment and ageing set the strength of a metal after shaping.
